correctness.rationale: The intrinsic rank-one left-multiplier locus is exactly a union of full false-twin blocks, because distinct nonzero binary neighborhood vectors are pairwise nonproportional. A linear isomorphism permutes these maximal subspaces. Product identities force equal-norm orthogonal columns, quotient-graph automorphism, positivity and t_j=t_i²/d_i. Connectedness gives one or two alternating scalings and regularity or bipartite biregularity. Conversely scalar/orthogonal block maps satisfy all natural-basis products. The proof addresses one-class and disconnected-quotient edge cases by requiring connected G with at least one edge; all degrees positive. Independent exact-rational checks reconstruct examples and degree conditions on all connected labeled graphs through six vertices.

value.rationale: The result gives the missing necessary condition in an explicitly motivated open classification, uniformly for every connected graph with singular false-twin quotient including twin-free singular graphs. It replaces determinant restrictions by intrinsic rank-one multiplication geometry and yields a complete closed normal form for all real isomorphisms. It is not a routine case of the earlier nonsingular result, and resolves the isomorphism criterion in combination with the previously treated complementary case.
